picked.title: End-to-End Image-Goal Navigation for Agile Quadrotors via Recurrent State Distillation
picked.summary: Image-goal navigation asks a robot to reach the viewpoint of a target photograph without a map or goal pose. In three dimensions, this requires not only recognizing the goal but also estimating 3D displacement and generating continuous control actions to approach and settle at the target view. This is difficult because the same visual difference between current and goal image can require very different actions depending on the robot's velocity, yet monocular images alone reveal neither metric scale nor body motion. As a result, existing image-goal policies are limited to planar action spaces and rely on a state estimator for flight control. Policies that map directly from images to low-level control commands have been demonstrated for agile flight, but not toward goal images in unseen environments. We present the first image-goal navigation policy that directly commands thrust and angular rates for agile quadrotor flight in unseen 3D environments, without relying on state estimation (e.g., SLAM, VO, or SfM) or a separate velocity controller. We train a recurrent vision-based policy through a four-stage pipeline that combines geometric and motion supervision with privileged-teacher distillation and end-to-end reinforcement learning fine-tuning. On 1000 held-out flights in unseen environments, the policy achieves an 82.3% success rate with a mean terminal position error of 0.10m across successful flights. Deployed zero-shot on a real quadrotor, the policy reaches an 84% success rate over 25 trials in an unseen indoor environment.

picked.title: Cairn: Object-Centric 3D Trajectory Priors for Steering Frozen VLAs
picked.summary: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) are capable low-level controllers, but they tie where objects go to the layouts they were trained on: when objects are moved or obstacles block the way, they carry them to the wrong place or into collisions. Fine-tuning on new layouts needs robot data for each one and erodes skills the model already has. We introduce Cairn, which keeps the VLA frozen and steers it at test time along learned 3D trajectories of the object in its gripper. A small prior reads point clouds of the scene and the held object, along with its pose when grasped and the instruction, and samples SE(3) trajectories up to its release that lead it around obstacles and turn it to fit through gaps. The prior and the VLA form the two levels of a hierarchical planner in which feedback runs both ways: the VLA's intended motion chooses and reshapes the trajectories, and the chosen one guides the VLA's denoising. Its predicted actions, mapped to the held object's poses through the grasp, are pulled toward the next waypoint, while the VLA's weights stay untouched. Across 1,941 held-out LIBERO scenes with displaced objects and obstacles, Cairn raises the success rate of a frozen π0.5 from 24.5% to 95.1%, above that of a π0.5 fine-tuned on our training layouts, without hurting standard LIBERO. On the third-party LIBERO-PRO benchmark, it raises success from 27.3% to 38.0%, and from 54.4% to 81.1% on the episodes it steers. On a real Franka, with a prior trained purely in simulation, it guides the frozen DROID π0.5 around an obstacle and to a placement at the limit of the arm's reach, where it otherwise fails. All code, models and data will be made public.

picked.title: HoloBrain-0.5 Technical Report
picked.summary: We present HoloBrain-0.5, a family of vision-language-action (VLA) models for manipulation across robot embodiments. The policies plan in a shared action space using robot state, kinematic structure, and calibrated camera observations. We standardize joint axes, coordinate frames, and tool-center points in robot descriptions (URDFs) and encode their kinematic graphs in a shared 3D representation. HoloBrain-0.5-Continuous generates action chunks by diffusion, while HoloBrain-0.5-Discrete uses residual finite scalar quantization (FSQ) and delayed autoregression. We pretrain both policies on over 10,000 hours of real-robot, simulation, and human-manipulation data spanning 15 embodiment categories. Across six closed-loop simulation settings, the discrete policy converges faster and reaches a higher mean success rate than the continuous policy (56.77% vs. 49.71%). On seven real-robot tasks, it achieves a mean progress score of 87.76% without task-specific post-training. After post-training, the continuous policy outperforms $π_{0.5}$ on the seven-task benchmark (94.52% vs. 86.25%) and an 11-task dual-arm benchmark (79.07% vs. 69.41%). The discrete-initialized continuous policy transfers five tasks zero-shot from Piper to Piper-X, scoring 63.28% on average. With target-robot demonstrations, the continuous policy scores 89.2% on Franka Panda and 92.94% on a mobile dual-arm platform. Although pretraining includes no Unitree G1 data, post-training with limited G1 demonstrations yields a mean progress score of 70.24% across three humanoid tasks, compared with 11.00% for $π_{0.5}$.

picked.title: Reference-Model-Guided Distributed MPC for UAV Swarm Formation Flying Under Switching Directed Graphs
picked.summary: Distributed formation control of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms in complex environments faces several challenges, including switching inter-agent connectivity, limited communication, external disturbances, and collision avoidance. To address these challenges, we propose a reference-model-guided distributed model predictive control (MPC) framework for UAV swarm formation. Each UAV uses relative-position information from its neighbors as input to a local reference model, whose output serves as the formation guidance for the onboard MPC controller. Meanwhile, a Kalman filter is utilized to predict neighboring UAV motions, enabling the construction of inter-UAV collision-avoidance constraints solely from instantaneous relative-state information. By decoupling MPC optimization from distributed coordination, this control architecture preserves the look-ahead planning and constraint-handling capabilities of MPC while enhancing the swarm's adaptability to switching directed graphs. Moreover, eliminating the exchange of neighbors' predicted trajectories reduces communication bandwidth demands, offering strong scalability for large-scale UAV swarms. To improve robustness and safety, disturbance-observer-based feedforward compensation is employed, while the bounded residual disturbance is explicitly considered in the control barrier function (CBF)-based obstacle-avoidance constraints. Finally, the proposed framework is validated through both simulations and real-world flight experiments. Specifically, the flight verification is conducted on a fully distributed multi-UAV platform without external global localization.

picked.title: 江行智能基模 CTO 陈龙：当「物理 AI 大脑」进厂，如何实现可靠落地？| ACM MM 2026
picked.summary: 工业现场不需要“最聪明”的模型，够用、可靠、可验证才是硬道理。在工业现场，模型识别出异常，只是第一步。 它还要把每一次传感器或相机观测对应到正确的设备、位置和任务状态，规划下一步行动，控制机器人完成操作，并验证动作是否真正满足了客户要求、规程和监管规则。 这正是工业物理AI与单纯感知系统之间的一道分界线：它不仅要感知环境、识别目标，还需要控制现实设备，并根据执行结果形成反馈。 在ACM MM 2026的一场国际工业物理AI研讨会（WIPAI 2026）上，江行智能基础模型CTO陈龙博士以《End-to-End Physical AI Closed-Loop Execution System for Industrial Applications》为题，详细介绍了面向工业应用的端到端物理AI闭环执行系统，并阐释了工业物理AI如何从“看得见”走向“动手做”。 在他看来，相较于开放环境，部署的工厂场景更稳定，任务也往往高度标准化。基础模型不必具备最强的通用智能，同样可以在工业现场可靠工作。在实际部署中更重要的，是在模型准确度与算力（服务器、GPU）成本之间做出合理取舍，而不是盲目追求超大模型。 在保留演讲原意的基础上，本文进行了编辑润色。 01 从“看见”到“做完”： 工业物理AI须打通执行闭环 …

picked.title: RoboScience 机器科学发布 GenSight：如何在一个模型，搞定生成和感知？
picked.summary: 热潮褪去之后，世界模型的研究该转向何处？今年上半年，世界模型是具身智能领域最风光的叙事。资本蜂拥而入，仿佛只要模型能把未来视频生成得足够逼真，机器人就自然能学会理解世界、规划行动。 热潮来得快，走得也快。问题首先出在概念本身，李飞飞团队今年 6 月专门撰文，说世界模型已经成为 AI 领域最重要、也最被滥用的术语之一。更根本的质疑来自实际效果，智源研究院院长王仲远说得很直接：视频生成模型可以生成一群猪在天上和飞机一起飞，因为训练数据里有科幻电影，它的目标从来就不是还原真实物理世界的规律。 9 月 GPT-6 Astra 发布后，大家发现，通用模型已经能覆盖具身的一部分能力，留给专门做世界模型的窗口期可能没多久了。融资市场的反馈更直接，纯讲世界模型故事的具身初创，已经很难再靠这个概念拿到钱。 在这个节点上，RoboScience 机器科学发布 GenSight ，看起来像是在逆势而行。 GenSight 做的事，简单说就是把视频生成和 4D 稠密感知塞进同一个预训练 Video DiT。给定一张初始图像和一句指令，它能生成机器人未来的操作视频，并同步输出每一帧的深度、具身分割和二维光流；给定一段已经拍好的操作视频，同一个模型也能在单次前向推理中直接读出几何、语义和运动信息。 读完论文，和 GenSight 核心成员聊过之后，雷峰网发现，这项工作不仅回应了世界模型被质疑的那几个要害，还给这个方向提供了一个值得认真对待的修正思路。 …

picked.title: Exploring nonlinear body oscillations for natural quadruped gaits
picked.summary: Schmidt et al. demonstrate that nonlinear normal modes can be used to develop natural, multi-gait locomotion in a compliant quadruped robot, leveraging its inherent mechanics. The approach offers a design tool to shape embodied intelligence in robotics.

picked.title: 具微科技高交会双新品首秀，全栈方案破解工业机器人连续作业难题
picked.summary: 11月26日，中国国际高新技术成果交易会（简称“高交会”）在深圳国际会展中心开幕。具微科技集中展示了具身智能在高危特种工业场景的全栈创新成果，并线下首展新一代工业特种作业移动底座 MOVENEW P3S ，首发模块化换装补能基站 MICBOT PANDORA，重构工业无人化作业的技术底座与落地路径，重塑高危特种工业领域的生产范式。 轮足复合移动底座，直面高危重载作业场景 开幕首日，具微科技展台迎来众多专业观众。现场四足机器人依次完成 360° 连续旋转、复杂地形跃障与定点跨障跳跃等动态演示，呈现整机运动性能；展台同期展出面向特种具身场景的新一代产品 MOVENEW P3S。 与多数以运动演示为主的四足机器人不同，P3S 面向工业高危环境设计，定位为可拓展的“工业特种作业移动底座”，而非单一巡检设备，可搭载检测、清障、搬运、处置等任务模块。 P3S 整机采用宽体短腿、四轮足构型，铺装路面优先以轮式模式巡航，复杂地形切换足式越障，支持原地转向；负载模式包括100 kg连续行走与爬楼、300 kg重载模式、400 kg低趴模式动态负载、600 kg静态极限负载等四种模式；轮式最高速度 5m/s，可通行 ±45° 坡道、35cm 连续台阶与 150cm 单级高台，本体防护等级 IP67、轮部 IP68，工作温度覆盖 -40℃～85℃，可适配防爆、防磁、防水、防冻等极端工况。 据具微科技相关负责人介绍，P3S 从底层 FOC 驱动到上层规划决策均为全栈自主研发，运动控制器闭环频率达 1000Hz 以上。MICPCI …
